chunks.arabic_text: يُوسُفُ بْنُ السَّخْتِ، بَصْرِيٌّ. ضَعِيفٌ، مُرْتَفِعُ الْقَوْلِ، اسْتَثْنَاهُ الْقُمِّيُونَ مِنْ «نَوَادِرِ الْحِكْمَةِ».

translations.en: Yūsuf ibn al-Sakht. Basran. Weak, a proponent of irtifāʿ in doctrine, the Qummis excluded him from “Nawādir al-Ḥikma”.

en.summary: Yūsuf ibn al-Sakht, a Basran narrator, is classified as weak (ḍaʿīf) due to his high opinion of himself (irtifāʿ al-qawl), a trait often associated with theological arrogance or sectarian pride. Notably, the Qummis scholars, who generally revered Nawādir al-Ḥikma, excluded him from this collection, highlighting a specific scholarly critique of his reliability or doctrinal alignment within the Shia tradition.
en.seo_question: Who is Yūsuf ibn al-Sakht and why was he excluded from Nawādir al-Ḥikma?

key_terms.يُوسُفُ بْنُ السَّخْتِ: Yūsuf ibn al-Sakht, the narrator being described
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak, a technical term in hadith sciences indicating a narrator of lesser reliability
key_terms.مُرْتَفِعُ الْقَوْلِ: Proponent of irtifāʿ (elevation), referring to a theological doctrine
key_terms.نَوَادِرُ الْحِكْمَةِ: Nawādir al-Ḥikma, a specific hadith collection
